Peripheral autonomic nerve dysfunction defines disease; altered visceral regulation does not establish direct damage to those organs.
Defined multisystem proteinopathy involving skeletal muscle, Paget bone lesions and optional frontotemporal neurodegeneration; cognitive impairment reported in 2/5.

Tumor arises in ovarian surface/stroma; reproductive organs have no axis. Mesothelioma histology does not establish pleural disease.
Defining tumors arise in adrenal medulla and autonomic paraganglia. Renal carcinoma and GIST are separate tumor risks; hypertension alone does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Inherited transaminase deficiency causes neurodevelopmental impairment, microcephaly and spasticity. Contractures occur in 3/14, below threshold.

White matter disease with cognitive and neurologic dysfunction defines condition. Hypertension is 1/5; hypertensive retinopathy is secondary rather than direct leukodystrophy damage.
Neurodevelopmental white matter disorder; persistent strabismus and scoliosis each reported in 4/4 assessed patients. Isolated mitral prolapse lacks support for common involvement.
Generic inflammation of vulva and vagina, both reproductive sites; an infectious or immune-mediated cause is not specified.
Bilateral skeletal enchondromatosis involving clavicles and long bones defines disease.
Prolactin-producing anterior pituitary neoplasm; visual pathway injury is not common across the entire tumor group.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood; organ enlargement alone does not establish common functional injury outside the hematologic axis.
Congenital corticospinal motor control disorder causing persistent mirror movements; muscle and skeletal damage are not defining features.
Developmental malformation of blood vessels; additional organ involvement depends on subtype and location.
Inherited structural skin fragility with recurrent blistering. Substantial mucosal and other organ injury varies by subtype and is not established across most patients.
Localized calcium deposition in tracheal tissue; no systemic metabolic disorder is specified.
Inherited susceptibility to bipolar mood disorder; purely psychiatric disease has no axis despite the neurological ancestor.
Hair shaft abnormalities, sparse brittle hair and dry skin define disease; sparse eyelashes do not establish ocular damage.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection directly inflames the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis.
